axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axes.assessment: C1–C6 are substantively addressed, as are the six negative constraints. The final retains one trusted offline file, fictional Rust/local SQLite, existing UI, weekly named-zone recurrence crossing DST, a single occurrence action, an existing exception and opaque content. It gives a concrete identity/edit sketch and distinguishes a preview horizon from stored recurrence. Rejecting RDATE/multi-day patterns is an explicitly declared first-release subset, allowed by the brief; it is not a demand to support every recurrence form. Existing-target and unrelated exceptions are handled distinctly. Owner choices are proposed contracts, not implementation claims. No extra application, service, account operation or deployment obligation was invented.

axes.name: Consequential source claims and exact applicability conditions
axes.assessment: Independently retrieved governing RFC text, Verified Erratum 4271, Google/Graph operation/resource documentation and versioned library/history evidence. Final original-slot identity, exclusion precedence, named-zone behavior, generated-gap correction, fold policy, exact/nominal duration distinction, INTERVAL default, COUNT/UNTIL mutual exclusion and UTC UNTIL condition are supported. Types and operation domains remain distinct: Graph originalStart is UTC DateTimeOffset; provider event IDs are not ICS identity; Graph boundaries are not file rules; API/ITIP messaging is not a file export. Raw-byte preservation/upsert/tombstones are labeled product designs. The Python history summary omits narrow conditions and a blanket provider-messaging sentence is broader than the detailed operation table; neither drives a consequential unsupported final decision. All 21 consequential claim records are in source-map.json.

axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, alternatives, history and opportunity breadth
axes.assessment: Discovery supplies actionable mechanisms rather than generic caution: original-slot detached exceptions; EXDATE snapshot exclusion versus iTIP organizer messaging; Google immutable original-slot fields versus Graph event/resource distinctions; Graph adjacent-occurrence-day restriction; raw component editing versus typed reserialization; exact versus nominal durations; and duplicate/import collision handling. Competing Rust leads have different compatibility tradeoffs: strict typed recurrence in caldata 0.17.3, byte-faithful/calendar-owned timezone architecture advertised by unpinned pimalaya/ical, and archived parser-only ical 0.11.0. Tagged Python icalendar history gives real opaque-value, URI-parameter and timezone regressions that motivate discriminating tests without alleging Rust defects. RDATE/multi-day recurrence remain optional future capabilities, and zone authority, crate choice and tombstone consumer behavior are investigated owner decisions. Breadth is adequate for this deliberately bounded feature; no full calendar/service research is required.

axes.name: Wrong criticism/corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axes.assessment: Every critic item F1–F4 and U1 has an explicit disposition, checked against primary evidence rather than critic agreement. F1/F2 correct real lineage source defects. F3 removes an actual representational ambiguity without alleging executed-code failure. F4 fills conditional grammar acceptance constraints rather than inventing a requirement to accept UNTIL. U1 remains honestly unverified, with concrete representation, preservation, observable checks and conditional test/defer choices. All 21 substantive exact plan sentences are mapped below, including the originally unspecified occurrence-key choice and all seven fixture classes. The final paraphrases the ambiguous first idea as current-start identity, a minor attribution overstatement; the chosen original-slot resolution is sound and requested. No materially wrong rejection or adopted correction remains.

axes.name: Supported meaning preserved across discovery/draft/critique/final
axes.assessment: The final remains self-contained and preserves the supported original-slot identity, master retention, exclusion/override distinctions, named-zone/DST model, preview-only expansion, existing-exception merge, raw owning-component property preservation, repeat-import/conflict design, provider operation comparison, all library/history leads and optional/owner choices. It does not replace science with predecessor IDs or merely enumerate edits. The original discovery/draft gap-skip statement is deliberately corrected, not silently regraded; unknown-property preservation remains required while its RFC attribution is narrowed. Duration and end-rule constraints are strengthened. The optional cancelled detached tombstone representation from early discovery is resolved into an explicitly local proposed EXDATE/removal/tombstone policy with retained consumer uncertainty; no proven alternate capability is erased. All original validation fixture classes and scope constraints survive.

axes.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.assessment: The final matrix has observable invariants for all required fixtures and additions: stable UID/original typed RID, no original phantom or duplicate override, one exclusion with master/neighbors intact, fixed local 18:30 with changing resolved offsets, preservation of raw opaque values/parameters/multiplicity/ownership, exact/nominal duration meaning, repeat-import stability, and no partial writes on unsupported/conflicting input. Generated-gap/count expectations are corrected using the verified erratum. Implementation, parser/exporter, SQLite, provider and independent-reader tests are explicitly proposed and unrun, consistent with the original assignment. Source rechecks and input hashes are research/provenance evidence only. A same-parser round-trip can expose regressions but is a weak self-oracle; it cannot prove live/provider compatibility, raw-byte preservation or a different reader. Independent permitted consumers and pinned-release fixtures are prospective compatibility oracles. Lack of nonexistent deployment tests is not a failure of this planning assignment.

sources.title: RFC 5545 iCalendar
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 5545, September 2009, with R02/R03 for verified errata
sources.governing_conditions: UID is TEXT and identifies the component; RECURRENCE-ID defaults to DATE-TIME, matches master value type/local form, and identifies the original slot. EXDATE wins over RRULE/RDATE inclusions; duplicates collapse; an unsynchronized DTSTART/rule is undefined. INTERVAL is positive and defaults to 1. COUNT includes DTSTART; COUNT and UNTIL are mutually exclusive; UNTIL for TZID DATE-TIME DTSTART is UTC DATE-TIME and is inclusive. Missing recurrence fields derive from DTSTART. A matching VTIMEZONE must cover recurrence instances. Folds use the first instant; gaps use the preceding offset. DTEND gives exact recurrence duration; DURATION gives nominal duration, with day/week components differing across transitions. §3.2.20 preserves unknown VALUE-type data; generic readers may ignore extension properties. New VEVENTs need UID/DTSTAMP and, without METHOD, DTSTART.
sources.applicability: Governs the offline interchange design. Product subset, raw-byte preservation, upsert keys, tombstones and UI input rejection are product decisions. The earlier skip-gap text must be read with R03 and the later computed-time paragraph.
sources.observation: Independent read-only HTTP retrieval and semantic inspection of relevant surrounding primary context; no downloaded code executed.
